spots.name: Atomium
spots.summary: The Atomium is a landmark modernist building in Brussels, Belgium, originally constructed as the centrepiece of the 1958 Brussels World's Fair.

spots.name: Grand-Place
spots.summary: The Grand-Place or Grote Markt is the central square of Brussels, Belgium. It is surrounded by opulent Baroque guildhalls of the former Guilds of Brussels and two larger edifices: the city's Flamboyant Town Hall, and the neo-Gothic King's House or Bread House building, housing the Brussels City Museum.

spots.name: Manneken Pis
spots.summary: Manneken Pis is a landmark 55.5 cm (21.9 in) bronze fountain sculpture in central Brussels, Belgium, depicting a puer mingens: a nude boy urinating into the fountain's basin.

spots.name: Jeanneke Pis
spots.summary: Jeanneke Pis is a modern fountain sculpture in central Brussels, Belgium. It was commissioned by Denis-Adrien Debouvrie in 1985 and erected in 1987 as a counterpoint to the city's famous Manneken Pis.

spots.name: Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula
spots.summary: The Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula, usually shortened to the Cathedral of St. Gudula or St. Gudula by locals, is a medieval Catholic cathedral in central Brussels, Belgium.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula

spots.name: Cinquantenaire
spots.summary: The Parc du Cinquantenaire or Jubelpark is a large urban public park of 30 ha in the easternmost part of the European Quarter in Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: Brussels Town Hall
spots.summary: The Town Hall of the City of Brussels is a landmark building and the former seat of that municipality of Brussels, Belgium. It is located on the south side of the Grand-Place/Grote Markt, opposite the King's House or Bread House building, housing the Brussels City Museum.

spots.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium are a group of art museums in Brussels, Belgium.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

spots.name: Royal Palace of Brussels

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Palace of Brussels is the official palace of the King and Queen of the Belgians in the centre of the nation's capital, Brussels. However, it is not used as a royal residence, as the king and his family live in the Royal Palace of Laeken in northern Brussels.

spots.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Basilica of the Sacred Heart is a Catholic minor basilica and parish church in Brussels, Belgium. It is dedicated to the Sacred Heart, inspired by the Basilique du Sacré-Cœur in Paris.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels

spots.name: Cinquantenaire Arcade

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cinquantenaire Arcade is a memorial arcade in the centre of the Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark in Brussels, Belgium. The centrepiece is a monumental triple arch known as the Cinquantenaire Arch.

spots.name: Mini-Europe
spots.summary: Mini-Europe is a miniature park located in the Bruparck entertainment park, at the foot of the Atomium, in Brussels, Belgium. Mini-Europe has reproductions of monuments in the European Union and other countries within the continent of Europe on display, at a scale of 1:25.

spots.name: Bourse Palace
spots.summary: The Bourse Palace, often simply called the Bourse, is a former stock exchange building in Brussels, Belgium. It was previously the seat of the Brussels Stock Exchange (BSE). Since 2023, its upper floors have housed the Belgian Beer World museum.

spots.name: Espace Léopold
spots.summary: The Espace Léopold or Leopoldruimte is the complex of parliament buildings in Brussels, Belgium, housing the European Parliament, a legislative chamber of the European Union (EU).

spots.name: Brussels City Museum
spots.summary: The Brussels City Museum is a municipal museum on the Grand-Place/Grote Markt of Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: Palace of Justice, Brussels
spots.summary: The Palace of Justice of Brussels or Law Courts of Brussels is a courthouse in Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries
spots.summary: The Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries is an ensemble of three glazed shopping arcades in central Brussels, Belgium. It consists of the King's Gallery, the Queen's Gallery and the Princes' Gallery.

spots.name: Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History
spots.summary: The Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History, also known as the Royal Military Museum, is a military museum that occupies the two northernmost halls of the historic complex in the Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark in Brussels, Belgium.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History

spots.name: Brussels-Central railway station
spots.summary: Brussels-Central railway station is a railway and metro station in central Brussels, Belgium. It is the second busiest railway station in Belgium and one of three principal railway stations in Brussels, together with Brussels-South and Brussels-North.

spots.name: Mont des Arts
spots.summary: The Mont des Arts or Kunstberg, meaning "Hill/Mount of the Arts", is an urban complex and historic site in central Brussels, Belgium, including the Royal Library of Belgium (KBR), the National Archives of Belgium, Square – Brussels Convention Centre, and a public garden designed by the landscape architect René Pechère.

spots.name: Place de la Bourse, Brussels
spots.summary: The Place de la Bourse or Beursplein, meaning "Stock Exchange Square", is a major square in central Brussels, Belgium. It was created following the covering of the river Senne (1867–1871). Nowadays, it is, after the Grand-Place/Grote Markt, the second most important square in the city.

spots.name: Hôtel Tassel
spots.summary: The Hôtel Tassel, also known as the Tassel House, is a historic town house in Brussels, Belgium. It was designed by Victor Horta for the scientist and professor Emile Tassel, and built between 1892 and 1893, in Art Nouveau style.

spots.name: Stoclet Palace
spots.summary: The Stoclet Palace, also known as the Stoclet House, is a historic mansion in Woluwe-Saint-Pierre, a municipality of Brussels, Belgium. It was designed by the Austrian-Moravian architect Josef Hoffmann for the Belgian financier Adolphe Stoclet, and built between 1905 and 1911, in the Vienna Secession style.

spots.name: Church of Our Lady of Laeken

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Our Lady of Laeken is a Catholic parish church in the Brussels district of Laeken, Belgium. Built in neo-Gothic style, it was originally erected in memoriam of Queen Louise-Marie, wife of King Leopold I, to the design of the architect Joseph Poelaert. It is dedicated to Our Lady of Laeken.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Our Lady of Laeken

spots.name: Church of Our Lady of Victories at the Sablon
spots.summary: The Church of Our Lady of Victories at the Sablon, or the Church of Our Lady of the Sablon, is a Catholic church in the Sablon/Zavel district of Brussels, Belgium. It is dedicated to Our Lady of the Sablon.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Our Lady of Victories at the Sablon

spots.name: Pentagon
spots.summary: The Pentagon or Brussels' city centre is the historical city centre of Brussels, Belgium, within the contours of the Small Ring inner ring road. The Small Ring is located on the site of the second walls of Brussels, which were built in the 16th century.

spots.name: Europa building
spots.summary: The Europa building is the seat of the European Council and Council of the European Union, located on the Rue de la Loi/Wetstraat in the European Quarter of Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: Church of St. Nicholas
spots.summary: The Church of St. Nicholas is a Catholic church in central Brussels, Belgium. Founded around 1125, it is one of the first four churches in Brussels and the best preserved in its successive developments. It is dedicated to Saint Nicholas.

spots.name: Magritte Museum
spots.summary: The Magritte Museum is an art museum in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium, dedicated to the work of the surrealist artist René Magritte. It is one of the constituent museums of the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium.

spots.name: Het Zinneke
spots.summary: Het Zinneke, sometimes called Zinneke Pis by analogy with Manneken Pis, is a bronze sculpture in central Brussels, Belgium, erected in 1999. Created by Tom Frantzen, it represents a dog urinating against a bollard, along the same lines as Manneken Pis and its derivative Jeanneke Pis.

spots.name: Palace of Coudenberg
spots.summary: The Palace of Coudenberg was a royal residence situated on the Coudenberg or Koudenberg, a hill in what is today the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: Art & History Museum
spots.summary: The Art & History Museum is a public museum of antiquities and ethnographic and decorative arts located at the Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark in Brussels, Belgium. The museum is one of the constituent parts of the Royal Museums of Art and History (RMAH) and is one of the largest art museums in Europe.

spots.name: Place Royale, Brussels
spots.summary: The Place Royale or Koningsplein is a historic neoclassical square in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium.

spots.name: King's House
spots.summary: The King's House or Bread House is a historic building in Brussels, Belgium, housing the Brussels City Museum. It is located on the north side of the Grand-Place/Grote Markt, opposite the Town Hall.

spots.name: World Trade Center
spots.summary: The World Trade Center (WTC) is a complex of skyscrapers at the corner of the Boulevard du Roi Albert II/Koning Albert II-laan and the Boulevard Simon Bolivar/Simon Bolivarlaan in the Northern Quarter central business district of Brussels, Belgium. Its three towers are among the tallest buildings in Belgium.

spots.name: Autoworld
spots.summary: Autoworld is an automobile museum in Brussels, Belgium. The museum displays a large and varied collection of over 300 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles from various eras, retracing the history of the industry from its birth in the 19th century to the modern age.

spots.name: La Monnaie
spots.summary: The Royal Theatre of La Monnaie is an opera house in central Brussels, Belgium. The National Opera of Belgium, a federal institution, takes the name of this theatre in which it is housed—La Monnaie in French or De Munt in Dutch—referring to the building as well as the opera company.

spots.name: Bruxella 1238
spots.summary: Bruxella 1238 is an archaeological site located beneath the Bourse Palace in Brussels, Belgium. The site presents the remains of a Recollect convent established in the early 13th century and offers visitors an insight into nearly a millennium of Brussels’ history.

spots.name: Musical Instruments Museum
spots.summary: The Musical Instruments Museum (MIM) is a music museum in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium. It is part of the Royal Museums of Art and History (RMAH) and is internationally renowned for its collection of next to 10,000 instruments.

spots.name: Ancienne Belgique
spots.summary: The Ancienne Belgique (AB) is a concert hall for contemporary music in Brussels, Belgium. Located in the historic heart of Brussels, it is one of the leading concert venues in Belgium, hosting a wide variety of international and local acts. Some 300,000 people attend a concert at the "AB" every year.

spots.name: Church of St. James on Coudenberg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. James on Coudenberg is a Catholic church on the historic Place Royale/Koningsplein, in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium. It is dedicated to Saint James, one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St. James on Coudenberg

spots.name: Oldmasters Museum
spots.summary: The Oldmasters Museum is an art museum in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium, dedicated to Old Master European painters of the 15th to the 18th centuries, with some later works. It is one of the constituent museums of the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium.

spots.name: Boulevard Anspach
spots.summary: The Boulevard Anspach (French) or Anspachlaan (Dutch) is a central boulevard in Brussels, Belgium, connecting the Place de Brouckère/De Brouckèreplein to the Place Fontainas/Fontainasplein.

spots.name: Forest National
spots.summary: Forest National (French) or Vorst Nationaal (Dutch) is a multi-purpose arena located in the municipality of Forest in Brussels, Belgium. The arena can hold more than 8,000 people. It hosts indoor sporting events as well as concerts by a wide variety of artists.

spots.name: Train World
spots.summary: Train World is a railway museum in Schaerbeek, a municipality of Brussels, Belgium, and the official museum of the National Railway Company of Belgium (NMBS/SNCB). It is situated in the preserved buildings of Schaerbeek railway station and in a new shed built to its north.

spots.name: Royal Library of Belgium
spots.summary: The Royal Library of Belgium is the national library of Belgium. The institution owns several collections of historical importance, like the Library of the Dukes of Burgundy, and is the depository for all books ever published in Belgium or abroad by Belgian authors.

spots.name: Congress Column
spots.summary: The Congress Column is a monumental column in Brussels, Belgium, commemorating the National Congress of 1830–31 and the establishment of the Belgian Constitution.

spots.name: Centre for Fine Arts
spots.summary: The Centre for Fine Arts is a multi-purpose cultural venue in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium. It is often referred to as BOZAR in French or by its initials PSK in Dutch.

spots.name: Hôtel van Eetvelde
spots.summary: The Hôtel van Eetvelde is a historic town house in Brussels, Belgium. It was designed by Victor Horta for Edmond van Eetvelde, administrator of Congo Free State, and built between 1895 and 1898, in Art Nouveau style. It is located at 4, avenue Palmerston/Palmerstonlaan in the Squares Quarter.

spots.name: South Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The South Tower or Midi Tower is a 38-storey, 150 metres (490 ft) office skyscraper built between 1962 and 1967 in Brussels, Belgium. The tower is the tallest building in Belgium, and was the tallest in the European Economic Community (EEC) upon completion, until it was surpassed by Tour Montparnasse in Paris in 1972.

spots.name: Egmont Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Egmont Palace, also sometimes known as the Arenberg Palace, is a neoclassical palace in Brussels, Belgium. It was originally built between 1548 and 1560 for Countess Françoise of Luxembourg and Count Lamoral of Egmont, though its appearance was heavily modified in the 18th and 19th centuries.

spots.name: Place de Brouckère
spots.summary: The Place de Brouckère or De Brouckèreplein is a major square in central Brussels, Belgium. It was created following the covering of the river Senne (1867–1871), replacing the Temple of the Augustinians, which was demolished in 1893.

spots.name: Palace of Charles of Lorraine

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of Charles of Lorraine is a neoclassical palace in the Royal Quarter of Brussels, Belgium. It was originally built between 1757 and 1766 for the Governor of the Habsburg Netherlands, Prince Charles Alexander of Lorraine, replacing the Palace of Orange-Nassau.

spots.name: Old England
spots.summary: The Old England department store was a large retailer in central Brussels, Belgium, partially housed in an Art Nouveau building constructed in 1899 by Paul Saintenoy out of girded steel and glass.

spots.name: Place du Luxembourg
spots.summary: The Place du Luxembourg or Luxemburgplein, meaning "Luxembourg Square", is a square in the European Quarter of Brussels, Belgium. It is better known by local European bureaucrats and journalists by one of its nicknames, Place Lux or Plux.

spots.name: Belgian Comic Strip Center
spots.summary: The Belgian Comic Strip Center, also known as the Comic Art Museum, is a museum in central Brussels, Belgium, dedicated to Belgian comics. It is located at 20, rue des Sables/Zandstraat, in an Art Nouveau building designed by Victor Horta to house the former Magasins Waucquez.

spots.name: Halle Gate
spots.summary: The Halle Gate is a former medieval city gate and the last vestige of the second walls of Brussels, Belgium. Built in the 14th century, it was heavily restored in the 19th century in its current neo-Gothic style by the architect Henri Beyaert.

spots.name: Rue d'Aerschot
spots.summary: The Rue d'Aerschot or Aarschotstraat is a street in the Schaerbeek municipality of Brussels, Belgium. It is known as a hotspot of the city's underground nightlife and famous for its brothels. The street is also known for its inexpensive lodging.

spots.name: Great Synagogue of Europe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Synagogue of Europe, formerly known as the Great Synagogue of Brussels, is the main synagogue in Brussels, Belgium, which was dedicated as a focal point for European Jews in 2008.

spots.name: Royal Crypt
spots.summary: The Royal Crypt lies underneath the Church of Our Lady in the Brussels district of Laeken, Belgium. It is the official burial place of the Belgian royal family, including all the Kings of the Belgians and their wives.

spots.name: Tour & Taxis

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Old industrial site, converted to multi use. Including a food market, business center, shops.

spots.summary: The construction of the halls started in 1935, when 5 halls were built for the 1935 World Fair. Hall 5, informally known as the Centenary Palace, was the most ornamental of the first 5 halls and is still in use. spots.name: Museum of Original Figurines
spots.summary: Belgium has a rich history of comics and comic characters, with titles like Suske en Wiske, Jommeke and Kiekeboe known by all Belgian children. Comic character figurines are popular, and the come to life in the museum. Visitors are immersed in the third dimension of the 9th art through a unique collection of comic book figurines. The collection is accessibly presented to a wider audience of young

spots.name: Charles Buls Fountain
spots.summary: Statue of Charles Buls, mayor of Brussels from 1881 until 1899. Charles was a prominent defender of equal rights, an intellectual, writer and widely regarded as the greatest mayor in modern history of the city. As son of a jeweler, young Charles was gifted with creativity and intelligence, and taught himself several languages including Latin and French. From 1879 he was elected into the Brussels c

spots.name: St. Gorik Hall
spots.summary: The hall is a former covered marketplace in the middle of St. Gorik Square, and in use as event space and temporary exposition area. Their history dates back to the early days of Brussels, when at its location, multiple small islands existed in the Zenne, the river flowing through (and nowadays underneath) the city. spots.summary: Guided tours not available. Presentations available for groups of 15 or more, booked in advance.

Manneken Pis Wardrobe
spots.summary: This small museum houses the wardrobe of Manneken Pis, Brussels' most famous statue. Because Manneken Pis has nearly 1000 different costumes, of which some historic specimens are sensitive to decay resulting from variations in temperature and humidity, only about 100 costumes are shown to visitors at a time. spots.name: European Council
spots.summary: Guided tours not available. Presentations available for groups of 15 or more, booked in advance.

spots.name: Museum of Erotics and Mythology
spots.summary: A small museum dedicated to the history of erotic art from antiquity until today. It is a private collection, one of the most attractive in Europe, housed in an 18th century house near the Sablon. On display are paintings, sculptures, Greco-roman antiquities, ivory, [[Japan

spots.name: Parlamentarium
spots.summary: The Parlamentarium is the visitors' centre of the European Parliament and is in the Parliament's Espace Léopold complex. The official opening was on 14 October 2011 by President of the European Parliament Jerzy Buzek. The permanent exhibition contains hundreds of multimedia components, explaining the European Parliament and other European Union institutions. The entrance to the centre is on the Pa
